solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In a number of sections, awful uproar in FT

indicators.note: in places the shuffled noise between the two letters of the newspaper's initials

parts.note: taken as written, the letters F and T

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of uproar are in a dreadful mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A noisy row breaks out inside the Financial Times, reported in instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the placing: the jumbled letters of 'uproar' (OURPAR) sit between F and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something divided into four parts is made up of several sections, a set number of them.

clue.text: Most outspoken diarist is French

parts.note: Anne Frank wrote a famous wartime diary
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A claim that some French diarist is the bluntest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means candid and direct, so the superlative is the most candid.

clue.text: College in Vilnius periodically recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so those letters are read in the backward direction
periodically takes every other letter of Vilnius, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A college in the Lithuanian capital remembered from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of Vilnius gives INU, which 'recalled' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is the informal short form of university, a place of higher education.

clue.text: Remove creases from papers

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like ironing out some documents; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: You press clothes with an iron, and newspapers and journalists are called the press.

clue.text: Bloke, Pole, Reg upset

parts.note: a pole is a rod

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the name is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A list of men: some bloke, a Polish man, and Reg who is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person beside the names, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodger is British slang for a man or fellow, a chap.

clue.text: Delayed returning: also others

indicators.note: returning tells us to read the word for delayed from right to left

parts.note: delayed means late

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for being late back, along with several others.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation et al. stands for 'and others', used to shorten a list of authors.

clue.text: To Rex, trusted adviser is a bully

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, king
a mentor is a trusted adviser

explanation.surface: Someone tells King Rex that his trusted adviser is a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor persecutes and harasses others, just as a bully does.

clue.text: Strike a light!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for hitting them

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the exclamation 'strike a light', an old expression of surprise; split it into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamp is British slang for punching someone, and a lamp is also a device giving light.

clue.text: Slum area's hospital within reach

indicators.note: within puts the hospital letter inside the phrase for reach

parts.note: to reach a place is to get to it

explanation.surface: A rundown district whose hospital is close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a deprived, overcrowded part of a city, often occupied by one group.

clue.text: What can add flavour to drink and sandwiches I observe

definitions.text: What can add flavour to drink

indicators.note: sandwiches means the word and is the bread with the next letters as filling

parts.note: taken as written
to observe is to see

explanation.surface: Advice on what gives a drink flavour, with an aside about sandwiches you have spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a mere link word but is the outer bread here, and the definition is a whole phrase rather than one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise plant tastes of liquorice and is used in drinks such as ouzo and pastis.

clue.text: Live in Her Majesty's female quarters

indicators.note: in places the word for live inside the royal abbreviation

parts.note: HM is the abbreviation for Her Majesty
to live is to be, and are is a form of be

explanation.surface: An invitation to reside in the Queen's women's quarters at the palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the separate part of a household, traditionally Muslim, reserved for the women.

clue.text: Gives up fun

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... a habit, abandons it

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it sounds like someone abandoning enjoyment; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick smoking is to quit it, and doing something for kicks means doing it for thrills.

clue.text: Play ball, throwing a rope, etc, around ring

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters on either side of the ring
throwing suggests the letters are tossed about and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a ring is round, the shape of O

explanation.surface: Instructions for a game involving throwing a rope and other things round a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play ball' looks literal, part of the game picture, but it is the idiom for working together.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for agreeing to work together, doing what others ask.

clue.text: Article in Ireland abridged: any one of two?

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the shortened country name
abridged means shortened, so the last letter of Eire is cut

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece in Ireland is cut down, and someone asks which of two is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Eire, the Irish name for the country, is a crossword favourite; 'abridged' trims its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Either refers to one or the other of a pair, whichever is chosen.

clue.text: Enthusiastically, dip tucked into early, but not starter

indicators.note: tucked into puts the dip inside what remains of early
not starter means the first letter of early is dropped

parts.note: a dip is a dent, a hollow

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly dips into an early meal, but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course, but 'not starter' means dropping the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and keen, so acting ardently is acting with great zeal.

clue.text: One demonstrating a bathroom fixture?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who shows something
second meaning: the spray device you wash under

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the word split as SHOW-ER, one who shows; the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower is a common plumbing fitting in a bathroom, and someone who exhibits things is literally a 'show-er'.

clue.text: Prime clientele vendor keeps hold of

indicators.note: keeps hold of says the words contain the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A trader holds onto his best customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' looks like an adjective for the customers but is the definition: a prime number.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is divisible only by itself and one, making it a prime number.

clue.text: Snooker player on break, maybe one making 26?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a snooker player compiling a break pots balls
second meaning: someone who makes pottery, such as the answer to 26 Across

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker a break is a run of pots, so the player making one is potting. The cross-reference points to 26 Across, CROCKERY, which a maker of ceramics produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter both sinks balls in cue sports and shapes clay into pots and dishes.

clue.text: Striker we hear needed for football

indicators.note: we hear says the word for striker is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a socker is one who socks, that is hits, someone

explanation.surface: A goalscoring forward is essential for a football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' looks like a footballer, but it means one who hits: a socker.
explanation.definitionFit: Soccer is the name for association football, used especially in America.

clue.text: Other people finally moving hither

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of people

explanation.surface: Other people are at last relocating to this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are formal words meaning to this place or to this point.

clue.text: Fuse taken out of transformer gently

indicators.note: taken out of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An electrician's advice to remove the fuse from a transformer carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse two things is to join them so they become one, which is what merging does.

clue.text: On reflection, being at home wearing raincoat is obsessive!

indicators.note: wearing means the raincoat goes around the reversed home word

parts.note: a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat

indicators.note: on reflection, like a mirror image, means the home word is written backwards

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone who wears a raincoat indoors is told they are obsessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' seems to govern the whole clue, but it turns only the short word for at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes frenzied, compulsive behaviour, as in a person fixated on something.

clue.text: Struggle with wife's opinion

parts.note: to vie is to compete, to struggle against
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband battles with his wife's point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal belief or way of seeing a matter.

clue.text: One class is angry

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
to class something is to rate it

explanation.surface: A school form that is collectively in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means furious, a stronger synonym for being cross.

clue.text: Dispute with jailbird before trial

indicators.note: before puts the jailbird ahead of the trial in the answer

parts.note: a con is a convict, a jailbird
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A convict argues his case ahead of his court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a claim is to challenge or argue against it.

clue.text: Watch we may receive, last of all

indicators.note: last of all takes the final letter of every one of the three words

explanation.surface: A watch is something we might get as a gift in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, to observe it.

clue.text: Minute steak's last for several days!

parts.note: minute (tiny) means wee, a Scottish word for small

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of steak

explanation.surface: A tiny steak takes an age to finish, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like a unit of time, which suits the definition, but here it means tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A week is a span of seven days, fairly described as several.

clue.text: Music fan visiting outskirts of city in China?

indicators.note: visiting puts the music fan inside the city's edge letters
outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of city

parts.note: a rocker is a fan of rock music

explanation.surface: A rock fan touring the suburbs of a city somewhere in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' seems to be the country; the question mark warns it is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain tableware is called china, and plates, cups and dishes together are crockery.
